This game is just hard enough to make you have to step away and come back after you have gathered your composure, or at least that was my experience. The game was fun, had you trying things over and over again, just to think, "there is no way I can do this in the amount of time allotted" just to then achieve the next level in the allotted time. It was frustrating at times, especially when you had to get your timing perfect in order to just miss being electrocuted or crushed. It was challenging but well worth the time invested!

What sets this apart and makes it a true indie classic is how I am able to replay it every now and then and realize just how exceptional the atmosphere and the design ideas are all over again. Every time it seems even better than I remember it. (I also have it for ps3, so my game time doesn't reflect how much I have played it.)

And I very much recommend trying to find the secret level and getting the hidden trophy. That level is very hard and immensely satisfiying to beat.

A massively popular game in the indie scene, enough to be ported to more than five game systems, LIMBO is a unique trip into a dark, surreal world. Everything is out to kill you and you only have your bravery, wits and skill to overcome the difficult trials ahead. A must-have for every gamer.

To read a more detailed review, please go to: http://breakingcanon.com/games/limbo/

A good original puzzle platformer with very interesting and unique visuals. However I did like the first half much more than I did the second because the atmosphere and exploration was what really made me love the first half. The second half became strictly a puzzle game and focused less on atmosphere and exploration with puzzle after puzzle in an industrial setting. It got very old towards the end and I just wanted it to be over which is not a good thing for a short game. The game also ends abruptly without no build up or climax just some gravity puzzles before the ending which was also disappointing. Those are my big complaints but it’s still good game and worth playing because of its originality.
7/10 (Good)

Absolutely crazy game! It had parts that were completely mind boggling and completely unexpected. A really decent platformer that really leaves the story to the imagination. Limbo is artistic, creative, and a blast to play. If you're into puzzle platformers where you don't have any shooting or run & gun mechanics, you'll really enjoy this game. It's a quick play, You could possibly beat it for the first time in about two hours. I've enjoyed myself with it a few times now. The achievements are not impossible but do require thought. I recommend this game for anyone who's looking for a few hours of awesome fun with a basic story and only five buttons... truly inspired.

FYI: watch out for the spider!

The experience of this game really sticks with you. I remember playing this game back when it came out, and I never really got around to finishing it. However, when I picked it back up again, I was able to vividly recall many of the impactful moments and devilish puzzles this game contains. Its bleak and lonely aesthetic really makes an impression.

The puzzles in this game definitely have a bit of a difficulty curve. I would also argue that a lot of the puzzle-related elements that are introduced later in the game are a detriment to its immersion. I started to feel a little bit disconnected from the world and found myself playing a run-of-the-mill puzzle game. Another issue is in the controls. The boy doesn't handle nearly as smoothly as he ought to for a game containing puzzles that require some level of precision. Many times did I have to repeat a simple puzzle because the boy grabbed onto something or jumped errantly to his own death.

I can forgive the shortcomings of this game mostly because of its length. If you're focused and are able to figure out puzzles easily, it's a 2-3 hour game. It's really short, moderately sweet, and immensely impactful for a 2D puzzle-platformer.

Just finished playing through this game. If you enjoy difficult puzzle platformers, this one is for you. The timing can be somewhat stingy late-game, but overall it's fair with deaths, and respawns are quick. The game's also fairly short, so buying it on sale is recommended.
It doesn't need those describtions or other stuff like advertising to tell any worthy gamer what "Limbo" is. It's a top-tier game in every aspect. A Masterpiece, made by true gods for poor mortals.

An eerie and absolutely beautiful little puzzle game with a Lord of the Flies feel to it. Found it very peaceful to play no raging needed as puzzles are simple enough. Very short but highly recommended.
Atmospheric little game, with amazing world-building and puzzles, that challenge you just enough, without breaking your brain. You should check it out!

10/10 I stumbled upon this gem here on sale for 1.99 on sale... talk about the deal of a century!! I love everything about this game... the visuals are my favorite and that fact that it is a atmosphere that many have tried to duplicate since and have not come close to truly pulling it off stands on its own ground all these years later. I have not played this game since its initial release on the xbox 360 back in the day and my first run through felt just as darkly enchanting as the first time i played the controls, visuals, audio, and pacing of the game are superb in making you feel very in control of your own fate, running through the game with less then 5 deaths makes you feel like your putting together an extremely beautiful dangerous puzzle and when your through you want to run through again just to experience its beauty and to share it with others... just do yourself a favor and buy this game, cause it's the literal definition of a classic and none of my words can do it justice... Just have patience! O and P.S. I was completely unaware of the extra "Hidden Area" in the game that was added to the steam and ps3 versions and was so stoked to just have some more hell to put myself through at the end :)

LIMBO is a standard side-scroller with some physics here-and-there, nothing too impressive. The story isn't well fleshed out, almost nonexistent, although the developers claim it's up to the gamer to interpret it. But considering how inconsistent the second half of the game felt compared to the first, I attribute it to laziness or lack of direction. However, LIMBO has some redeeming qualities--it's art style and music. The developers took a minimalist approach and chose only to us white, black, and gray. The environments are diverse and look beautiful to say the least. And the music, when it pops up, really grabs your attention and sets the mood. It was something I enjoyed listening to, so much so in fact that I bought the soundtrack.

The pros: A hauntingly beautifully puzzle platformer. Though it only took me 3.7 hours to complete, I enjoyed "nearly" every second of it (see cons). This game can be enjoyed by both novice and experienced gamers as it did not require much skill but did require you to think a little (especially in the later half). For $5 (on sale) it's a steal.

The cons: The controls are the only frustrating thing about this game. Controlling the game with one hand while eating a slice of pizza with the other worked for some RPGs but this is a platformer. It's one of those games where pressing "UP" makes you jump. While you can of course assign this to another button on your gamepad, you need to use the same button to climb up ladders. This means that you'll be rushing to climb up a later but instead your character will jump off and die.

Despite the negative rating but I actually do like this game.
BUT What I cannot really stand is its illogical way to present the puzzles, as to the player is rarely given the opportunity to recognize a danger and work out for a solution. The whole game is just a repetitive exercise of attempt-Death-Retry-Death-solution found-New Death. The death in LIMBO is not a punishment for the player's mistake, but the only possibility to find the solution to a puzzle. Frustration above satisfaction, you'll never solve a puzzle because you're good, but because you died enough to understand the only way to pass a section of the level.

My experience:
I played Limbo for a bit everyday and i liked it
It could be a bit frustrating at some points because you die a lot
So at some points it's not really solving a puzzle but dying until you get the right timing.

Despite the sometimes frustrating deaths, the game has a lot of good puzzles!
Also the art-style is lovely, it's really dark and simple but yet so beautiful and deep.

(There's also no option to change your keybinding, so you'll be playing with the good-old arrow keys)

Story:
There isn't really a proper story, you just get thrown into the game.
From what i can make out of it: You're a boy that's searching for his girlfriend (or sister) in this horrific world called the Limbo.

Conclusion:
If you love good puzzle games with a darkish art-style and can handle cheap deaths without destroying your keyboard
This will be the perfect game for you!
